chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Complaining about omissions; After Midnight credits; Lady Sings the Blues
summary: He jokes about shooting Hentoff and Feather, notes his After Midnight credit and film and stage work with Sinatra and Sammy Davis.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Maybe I will. I'll go out and shoot Nat Hentoff first, then I'll shoot Leonard. This is -- as I say, this is very disturbing. I can't understand this. You know, because I made records, two solos, like with the Nat -- this thing we did with Nat, with "After Midnight" that featured Stuff Smith, John Tizol, Willie Smith, Harry Edison, John Collins. And Nat. How can I -- you know, what is this? It's just amazing, I don't understand it.
(inaudible) you've been out there on the stage with Sinatra.
You were in Lady Sings the Blues.
I saw you on the screen.
That's right, and you also saw me on the stage with Sinatra.

That's right. I worked with Sammy Davis, I was featured with Sammy, you know, I had to accompany him, really. You know, just guitar and Sammy. These things I just don't understand what happens. You know. Maybe this will set the record straight. You know. I hope so, because this is very disturbing.
Another point, jazz scholars will go to the Smithsonian and find out about you but I hope something gets published, too,

Well, I hope so, because there is still a lot. When I sit down and really think, you know, and really think about incidents and things like that, you know, this is just off the top of my head right now, you know. I'm just rambling and reminiscing, but when I think back I'm wondering where was I supposed to be, you know. You know, what was I doing all of this time to get known? Or --
